entry.title: Federal judge blocks attempts to restrict mail-in voting
entry.content:
AUGUSTA, MAINE – A federal judge in Boston blocked the Trump administration from interfering with states’ rights to conduct mail-in voting for the upcoming November elections, now 67 days away. Judge Indira Talwani ruled yesterday that the plaintiffs were likely to succeed in proving the administration’s order was unconstitutional. 

“Last night’s decision was wonderful news for Maine voters who rely on absentee voting,” Secretary Bellows said. “The judge made clear that the states, not the federal government, are in charge of elections. That goes to the heart of our legal fights in court against the Trump Administration. We will continue to stand with other states and voting rights advocates across the nation to defend the voting rights – including the right to vote by mail – for every citizen.”

In the decision, Judge Talwani wrote, “the Constitution charges the States with election administration” going on to say that no law has been passed by Congress that “would permit the USPS to regulate election mail.” The judge went even further to note that with just two months to the election, it would an expensive and likely impossible task for the 2026 election, saying, “Plaintiff States face irreparable harm where they are required to comply with a likely unconstitutional regulation for which compliance is practically impossible.” 

###

entry.title: GEAR UP Week - September 21 through 25
entry.content:
WHEREAS, Gaining Early Awareness and Readiness for Undergraduate Programs (GEAR UP) is a federal grant program designed to increase the number of low-income students who are prepared to enter and succeed in postsecondary education and careers; and

WHEREAS, GEAR UP Maine was founded in 1998, and since then has helped prepare over 29,000 students to pursue education and career pathways they otherwise may not have been able to; and

WHEREAS, administered by the University of Maine Farmington and the nonprofit Syntiro, GEAR UP Maine supports students beginning in 7th grade through high school and onward as they prepare for college, careers, and lifelong success; and

WHEREAS, support provided by GEAR UP includes tutoring, mentoring, financial education, college scholarships, career exploration, and more; and

WHEREAS, GEAR UP Maine will serve 5,000 students in seventh through twelfth grade during the current grant period of 2023-2030; and

WHEREAS, Maine is committed to providing a high-quality education for all students and helping them reach their highest potential, no matter the path they choose;

NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim the week of September 21-25, 2026 as

GEAR UP Week

throughout the State of Maine, and I urge all citizens to recognize this observance.

In testimony whereof, I have caused 
the Great Seal of the State to be 
hereunto affixed GIVEN under my 
hand at Augusta this twenty seventh day 
of August Two Thousand Twenty-Six

entry.title: Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month - September
entry.content:
WHEREAS, ovarian cancer is the fifth leading cause of cancer deaths of women in the United States, and it causes more deaths than any other gynecologic cancer; and


WHEREAS, the American Cancer Society estimates that 21,010 cases of ovarian cancer will be newly diagnosed in 2026 and that 12,450 individuals will die from the disease nationwide, including 100 new cases and 70 deaths in Maine; and


WHEREAS, many people are unaware of the symptoms of ovarian cancer, which can often include bloating, pelvic or abdominal pain, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, urinary issues, and several more that are easily confused with other diseases; and

WHEREAS, the lack of an early detection test for ovarian cancer combined with its vague symptoms means that approximately 80 percent of cases of ovarian cancer are detected at an advanced stage; and

WHEREAS, all women are at risk for ovarian cancer, but approximately 20 percent of women who are diagnosed with ovarian cancer have a hereditary predisposition to the disease which places them at even higher risk; and

WHEREAS, the family history of a woman has been found to play an important role in accurately assessing their risk of developing ovarian cancer, and medical experts believe that family history should be taken into consideration during the annual well-woman visit of any woman; and

WHEREAS, ongoing investments in ovarian cancer research and education and awareness efforts are critical to closing these gaps and improving survivorship for women with ovarian cancer; 

NOW THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim September 2026 as 

Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month

throughout the State of Maine, and I urge all citizens to recognize this observance.

In testimony whereof, I have caused

the Great Seal of the State to be

hereunto affixed GIVEN under my

hand at Augusta this twenty seventh 
of August Two Thousand Twenty-Six

entry.title: Process for Authorizing Seasonal Migratory Game Bird Hunting
entry.content: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service or we) is changing the administrative process for authorizing seasonal migratory game bird hunting in the United States. Migratory game bird hunting regulations are currently promulgated annually to provide opportunities for recreation and sustenance; aid Federal, State, and Tribal governments in the management of migratory game birds; and allow harvests at levels compatible with migratory game bird population status and habitat conditions. The Service is adopting a more efficient administrative process for authorizing seasonal migratory game bird hunting. The Service will issue a memorandum to establish the limits and authorize seasonal migratory game bird hunting once every 3 years. The Service will continue to make annual decisions on harvest levels and will update the memorandum sooner than 3 years if changes are prescribed by our decision frameworks. The process eliminates the need for subsequent annual Federal regulation promulgation and rulemaking and is expected to increase efficiency; better meet State, Tribal, and Federal rulemaking constraints; and reduce the complexity and costs. Our goal is to better serve State partners and the hunting public while continuing to meet the legal and conservation purposes of the Migratory Bird Treaty Act. Tribes are already authorized under a similar process.

MaineCare Comprehensive Benchmarking Report Initiation Notice

Aug 31, 2026

The Department initiated a comprehensive rate benchmarking report, as required by MRS Title 22 §3173-J. Rate reform law requires that, every four years, the Department compare MaineCare rates to the rates paid by the following:

  • Medicare
  • At least five comparison Medicaid states
  • Any appropriate Maine commercial payers

Interested parties will have the opportunity for public review and comment. The final report will be available on the MaineCare Rate System Reform webpage.

For questions please contact Megan Scott, MaineCare’s Legislative and Reform Coordinator.

*This notice is provided pursuant to Public Law 2022, Chapter 639.

Section 45: Hospital Non-Claims Payment Schedule for October 2026

Aug 31, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) is preparing to launch an upgraded version of the Maine Integrated Health Management Solution (MIHMS), MaineCare’s claims processing system. To support a smooth transition, OMS must implement temporary system access limitations and adjustments to payment cycles in October.

MaineCare will distribute two separate hospital Prospective Interim Payments (PIPs) the week of September 28, 2026. MaineCare will not distribute PIPs the week of October 5, 2026.

For questions, please contact Amanda Lee, Rate Setting Coordinator.

Other System Access Limitations

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. Topics include:

  • October payment schedule
  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA)
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal
  • Paper & fax document submissions
  • Provider Services & Member Services call centers
  • Value Added Network (VAN) Trading Partners
  • Prior authorizations for prescriptions and behavioral health services
  • Electronic Visit Verification (EVV)

You can also check the OMS Provider Resources webpage, in the first box of information called “Health PAS Online Portal,” for the most recent information about the upgrade.

entry.content:

DHHS → Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) → Provider Resources → Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Aug 31, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training starting September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live.

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition.

Steps you need to take to attend training

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities.
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions.
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance.
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference.

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions

Course Name

Description

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users.

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality.

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities.

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC)

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources.

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility.

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login.
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account.
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window.
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address.
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript.
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile.
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods:
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email.
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event.
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink.

Do not forward meeting invitations to other attendees. Each participant must register through the LMS to receive course access, training

Attention Trading Partners: MIHMS Upgrade October Payment Cycle Changes and System Access Limitations

Aug 31, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) is preparing to launch an upgraded version of MIHMS, MaineCare’s claims processing system. The upgrade is currently scheduled to go live on October 10, 2026. To support a smooth transition, OMS must implement temporary system access limitations and adjustments to payment cycles in October.

From Friday, October 2 at 8:00 PM until Monday, October 12 at 8:00 AM, MIHMS will be in a “data freeze” while OMS completes final system readiness and transition activities.

Please note that we have updated the FAQ previously shared, as of August 31, 2026.

Changes to October payment cycles:

Review this information and plan billing accordingly to prepare for the transition.

Payment Impact

Claim Submission Deadline for Inclusion in Payment Cycle*

*As always, timely submission does not guarantee that the claim will process in time for the next payment cycle. OMS may take up to 30 days to process and pay a claim, depending on any edits or issues that may cause the claim to pend for manual review, as well as other processing requirements that may require the full 30-day timeframe.

Non-claims payments:

By September 1, OMS will communicate with any providers expecting non-claims payments that may be affected by the schedule described above.

Preparing for the changes to October payment cycles:

Beginning September 1, 2026 7:00 AM, OMS will return the HealthPAS Online Portal to its previous regular operating hours. Providers will again have 24/7 access to the portal, for additional flexibility and time to submit claims outside of standard business hours. 

We strongly encourage providers to submit claims approaching timely filing limits in the next few weeks to avoid potential submission delays. The planned data freeze does not modify existing Medicaid timely filing requirements. Providers remain responsible for ensuring claims are submitted within the established timely filing guidelines.

Other system access limitations:

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. We have updated the FAQ as of August 31, 2026. Topics include:

  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA)
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal
  • Paper & fax document submissions
  • Provider Services & Member Services call centers
  • Value Added Network (VAN) Trading Partners
  • Prior authorizations for prescriptions and behavioral health services
  • Electronic Visit Verification (EVV)

You can also check the OMS Provider Resources webpage, in the first box of information called “Health PAS Online Portal,” for the most recent information about the upgrade.

For questions or clarifications, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. Please note, Provider Services does not have additional information beyond what is shared in this message and in the FAQ linked above.

entry.title: National Park Service v. National Trust for Historic Preservation in the United States
entry.content:
_________________ _________________ 1 Cite as: 609 U. S. ____ (2026) Per Curiam SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES No. 26A203 NATIONAL PARK SERVICE, ET AL. v. NATIONAL TRUST FOR HISTORIC PRESERVATION IN THE UNITED STATES ON APPLICATION FOR STAY [August 31, 2026] PER CURIAM. In October 2025, the federal government started a project to replace the East Wing of the White House. The first phase involved the demolition of the existing East Wing, something the government completed in December 2025. The next phase, currently ongoing, involves the construc- tion of a new East Wing, including a below-ground military installation and an above-ground ballroom. The National Trust for Historic Preservation in the United States (Trust) filed a lawsuit in federal district court challenging various aspects of the project. As part of its suit, the Trust filed a motion on March 5, 2026, seeking a preliminary injunction. The injunction the Trust sought fo- cused not on the already-comp leted demolition of the old East Wing but on halting the ongoing construction of a new one. On March 31, 2026, the district court granted the Trust’s motion and issued a preliminary injunction. As later clari - fied, the injunction essentially permitted the government to continue work on the new below-ground military installa- tion but enjoined any further construction above ground, except as “strictly necessary” to protect the White House, the President, and his staff. entry.title: National Wildlife Refuge System; 2026-2027 Station-Specific Hunting and Sport Fishing Regulations
entry.content: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS or Service), open or expand hunting opportunities on 111 field stations, including 107 units of the National Wildlife Refuges System (Refuge System or NWRS) and 4 units of the National Fish Hatchery System (Hatchery System or NFHS). This includes opening hunting or sport fishing opportunities for the first time on 14 National Wildlife Refuges (NWR) and 3 National Fish Hatcheries (NFH). These actions will open or expand more than 1,450 opportunities for hunting and fishing across the NWRS and NFHS in order to increase access for the American public. In accordance with Secretary's Order (S.O.) 3447 and Director's Order (D.O.) 233, we also make changes to existing station-specific regulations in order to improve the clarity and accuracy of regulations, reduce the regulatory burden on the public, ensure consistency across FWS lands and waters, and comply with a Presidential mandate for plain-language standards.

entry.title: Pacer - Temporary Fee Increase Effective Jan. 1, 2027
entry.content:
Wednesday, September 2, 2026

On Jan. 1, 2027, a temporary increase in fees for electronic access to court records will take effect to help reimburse the costs of the development of the new case management and public access system. 

The increase of two cents per page, from 10 cents to 12 cents, was approved by the Judicial Conference’s Executive Committee on behalf of the Judicial Conference of the United States. In addition, the automatic exemption for PACER fees was raised from $30 to $40 per quarter, ensuring that most individual users (those who use $40 or less in PACER services per quarter) would continue to incur no fee or fee increase.

The fee increase will remain in place for a five-year period.

entry.title: New counsel memo: Standard of review for Right-to-Sue requests made before 180 days have passed
entry.content:
MEMO TO: Kit Thomson Crossman, Executive Director FROM: Barbara Archer Hirsch, Commission Counsel Colin R. Hurd, Deputy Commission Counsel DATE: July 23, 2025 RE: Standard of review for right-to-sue requests made before 180 days have passed As you are aware, 5 M.R.S. § 4612(6)(B), enacted in 2023, delineates the circumstances in which the Executive Director (“ED”) shall issue a right-to-sue letter (“RTS”) to a complainant who requests one before their complaint has aged 180 days with the Commission. Prior to the 2023 enactment, complainants could never request an RTS prior to 180 days. Now, the Commission “shall” issue an early RTS when two elements are concurrently met. First, the ED must determine that the complainant demonstrated good cause for requesting the RTS before the passage of 180 days, and second, the ED must certify that it is probable that the Commission will be unable to conclude its investigation before the 180 th day from the date on which the complaint was filed. After 180 days have passed, the complainant may request and receive an RTS without having to meet these standards. The second element of § 4612(6)(B) is relatively straightforward. The first element, however, is more nuanced. The Maine Human Rights Act does not define “good cause”. The Commission’s Procedural Rule provides that the Commission may grant extensions of certain time limits “for good cause shown”, 94-348 C.M.R. Ch. 2, § 2.11(C), but also do not define the term. In practice, the Commission requires that parties seeking extensions demonstrate that the requested extension is necessary due to extenuating circumstances, such as serious personal illness or a death in the family; inconvenience is insufficient to meet this standard.

entry.title: Trump’s Trade War with Canada is Not Maine’s
entry.content:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

You know, last summer I sat down for a cup of coffee at Tim Hortons in Caribou with Ron Turcotte, the legendary jockey who rode Secretariat to the Triple Crown in 1973. Ron Turcotte lived across the border in New Brunswick, Canada, but he picked up his mail at the U.S. Post Office in Van Buren, Maine, and did errands there.

His life showcased the reality of so many people living along the Maine-Canadian border. Yeah, there may be an international border there, but our communities, families, and economies are deeply entwined. And in places like the Saint John Valley, these connections existed long before the border ever did.

Throughout Maine, the President's trade war has driven up the cost of everything from groceries to cars and trucks and construction materials we need to build more homes. Because these tariffs are nothing more than taxes on American families and businesses.

Now the President has escalated his trade war, imposing 50 percent tariffs on many Canadian goods. And life is about to get more expensive and more complicated for Maine people, as well as Canadians.

In the Saint John Valley, about 90 percent of municipal road salt comes from Canada. And now, because of the President's new taxes, a major Canadian distributor has announced that it will halt deliveries of salt for the foreseeable future. It's not unheard of for The County to see snow in late September or early October, so this isn't some abstract trade war—the President's reckless behavior may soon threaten public safety.

And the damage to our state from the President's arbitrary and whiplash tariffs is not limited to business with Canada. In 2024, a developer wanted to create 125 new jobs in Jay, Maine, by turning that shuttered paper mill into an oriented strand board manufacturing facility. But the President's tariffs then increased the cost of importing specialized equipment from Europe so that developer was forced to scrap his plans.

President Trump claims his tariffs will bring manufacturing jobs back to America, but hey in Jay, his tariffs killed 125 of those jobs before they could even be created.

Now Canada is responding to the recent tariffs with tariffs of their own. Soon they'll add taxes to goods that last year made up $170 million of Maine's exports. These tariffs will make exporting these goods more expensive—hurting industries and communities that never asked to be caught in this fight. Industries and communities that, like Ron Turcotte's life, just do not fit neatly on one side of the border or the other.

As I record this, negotiators have not reached an agreement to avoid Canada's retaliatory tariffs from taking effect on September 8th. President Trump must de-escalate this ridiculous trade war before his recklessness does any more damage to the world economy and to Maine's economy.

We in Maine know that we share more than a border with Canada. We share an economy, a history. We share friendships and families and a way of life. Our relationship does not belong to any one president or one prime minister. It belongs to the everyday Mainers and Canadians who can pull up a chair at Tim Hortons, do business together, be friends, and lend a hand when a neighbor needs one.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Looking Ahead: Eligibility-Dedicated Data Feed to Support MaineCare Renewals and Enrollment

Sep 04, 2026

Two weeks ago, we announced communications support for MaineCare partners and providers regarding changes the federal government is making to MaineCare (Maine’s Medicaid program) eligibility. This message provides an early look at planned data-sharing that will help the Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) verify information needed for MaineCare eligibility. Our goal is to help eligible Mainers keep their coverage and access to services with as little disruption as possible.

No action is needed now. We are sharing this information early to make providers aware of what is being planned. We will share more information as plans and timelines are finalized.

DHHS will continue to use administrative data sources it has access to as much as possible to support automatic (“passive”) renewals for MaineCare members. Federal changes to eligibility mean we need additional information to help more eligible members maintain their MaineCare coverage. This data will help Mainers continue to benefit from MaineCare, which in turn will help providers minimize the impact of these federal Medicaid cuts on their revenue and on their charity and uncompensated care.

Clinical Data Will Help People Stay Enrolled in MaineCare

Electronic health record (EHR) systems contain clinical data that Maine and numerous other states are planning to use to help exempt Medicaid applicants and members with work-limiting health conditions from Work Requirements. In Maine, this data will support MaineCare eligibility determination activities administered by the Office for Family Independence (OFI). DHHS intends to partner with providers to collect this information through HealthInfoNet, the State’s contractor for this work. HealthInfoNet will identify indicators of exemptions from work requirements by collecting and processing this clinical data from providers. Using clinical data alongside claims and other administrative data to generate more timely and comprehensive information will help keep Mainers enrolled in MaineCare. We will refer to the data sent to HealthInfoNet for this purpose as the eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed.

Until the eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed is established we will be basing automatic exceptions for work-limiting health conditions on claims data alone in order to meet implementation deadlines.

This Data Sharing Will Be Separate from the Health Information Exchange

The eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed will be separate from the health information exchange (HIE) data that many providers already share with HealthInfoNet.

The eligibility-dedicated data feed will include only the information needed to support MaineCare eligibility activities. This information will be stored separately from HIE data. It will not be available through HealthInfoNet’s clinical portal or through analytics tools used by some provider organizations. The eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed will be used only in support of OMS and OFI activities associated with eligibility.

Key details to note:

  • The steps needed for a provider to establish this new data feed will vary by provider organization. For example, some provider organizations already have a data feed with HealthInfoNet that can be used as a starting point. Capabilities of the organization’s EHR vendor or technology support may also affect the work needed to establish the data feed. Providers eligible for relevant Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) funding may consider using this funding for these costs, as determined by the allowable uses of specific RHTP opportunities.
  • We expect it will take the majority of provider organizations two to four months to build their eligibility-dedicated clinical data feed with HealthInfoNet. This time range will be dependent on provider organization’s or vendor’s availability to engage with HealthInfoNet. We expect it will take less time than building a typical HIE data sharing connection with HealthInfoNet.
  • Clinical care teams are not expected to need to take additional steps to send this information as part of their day-to-day work. Once the data feed is established, the identified data categories will be shared automatically with HealthInfoNet.
  • Broad categories of exemptions in statute for work-limiting health conditions include those who are blind or disabled, have a substance use disorder, disabling mental disorder, or complex medical condition. DHHS continues to work with the federal government to clarify data related to these categories that may assist states to automatically exempt individuals, including information related to a person’s ability to work. Kinds of data may include demographic information, diagnosis indicators, encounter or event indicators, and billing codes, among others.

More Information Will Be Coming – No Action Needed Now The Department and HealthInfoNet will distribute instructions for provider organizations to opt into this initiative and implement the eligibility-dedicated data feed. Future communications will include information such as:

  • Which provider types will be prioritized for establishing these connections
  • How providers can participate
  • The types of information that will be needed
  • Technical requirements and specifications
  • Onboarding and implementation steps
  • Timelines
  • Testing procedures
  • Contacts for technical and operational qu

entry.title: Management Track Assessment for American Plaice and Gulf of Maine Haddock; Public Meeting
entry.content: NMFS will convene the Management Track Assessment Peer Review Meeting for the purpose of reviewing American plaice and Gulf of Maine haddock stocks. The Management Track Assessment Peer Review is a formal scientific peer-review process for evaluating and presenting stock assessment results to managers for fish stocks in the offshore U.S. waters of the northwest Atlantic. Assessments are prepared by the lead stock assessment scientist and reviewed by an independent panel of stock assessment experts. The public is invited to attend the presentations and discussions between the review panel and the scientists who have participated in the stock assessment process.
